notes: All configurations reproduce the published scored counts, passes, and task counts. The published pass@1 leaves out unscored attempts, so attempted-task pass rates are lower where a configuration has them.

The publisher leaves out routing, provider-timeout, verifier-timeout, upstream-provider, rate-limit, and unclassified errors. Routing failures end before the agent acts, but provider timeouts run far longer than scored attempts and verifier timeouts carry patches, so they are the system's attempts. The primary analysis counts all of them as failures, as the methodology requires without a supported conversion; excluding them is a sensitivity analysis.
Agent timeouts and context-window failures remain scored attempts; a few agent timeouts passed.
A few configurations have unequal attempts per task; the task-level model keeps equal task weights, and tasks without attempts are missing results, not failures.
Use trial observations or their aggregates, not both as independent data.

cost.basis: token prices listed for the five GPT-6 Astra effort settings, without a separate compute fee; other configurations state no basis
notes: Cost covers all attempts, including unscored ones, so a configuration is complete only when every attempt has a known cost.
Published cost means cover scored attempts with a known cost and differ from all-attempt means.
Missing costs fall on both unscored and scored attempts.

campaigns.run: publisher configuration name, one run per system
campaigns.protocol: 113 tasks under mini-swe-agent with one scoring rule
notes: Every configuration uses mini-swe-agent, so this source says nothing about harness differences.
Candidate shared systems connect it to both Terminal-Bench versions.
